A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching central framework, experiments, and appendix material. Text, equations, tables, and plots support reliable comparison. The conflicting vision-dataset descriptions in v2 create a localized uncertainty.

before.justification: v1 reports original layer-wise MTEB evaluations, representation measurements, training-checkpoint analyses, input-perturbation experiments, and vision-model results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds layer-selection results in Table 2 and a revised vision-model evaluation in Figure 14.

M1.justification: New Appendix E introduces an unsupervised layer-selection procedure: compute DiME, InfoNCE, or dataset entropy across layers and select the minimizing layer separately for each task. This adds a practical procedure to the existing representation-analysis framework; the underlying metrics and model architectures are unchanged.

E1.justification: The 32 MTEB tasks, WikiText data, and extreme-input scenarios are retained. v1 Section 6 specifies ImageNet-1k, whereas v2 Figure 14 specifies ImageNet-100 but v2 Section 6 still says ImageNet-1k. Consequently, the actual change in vision dataset and class coverage cannot be established reliably.

E2.justification: Figure 14 adds AIMv2 to the vision-model comparison. CLIP was already plotted in v1, despite being omitted from its main-text model list. New Table 2 also compares metric-based layer selectors with final-layer selection and a supervised best-layer reference.

E3.justification: The vision evaluation is substantially revised: v1 Figure 14 reports linear-probe top-5 accuracy, while v2 reports attention-probe top-1 accuracy and replaces the LiDAR panel with dataset entropy. Appendix E additionally introduces task-wise unsupervised selection evaluated against final-layer and supervised best-layer choices. These are changes in evaluation design, not directly comparable performance measurements.

E4.justification: Appendix E and Table 2 add a practical test of whether metric correlations support useful layer selection, comparing three selection criteria across two models. The earlier repetition, randomness, prompt-length, training-progression, scaling, and transformer-component analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing correlation reporting and Figure 5's variability display are retained; the new layer-selection and revised vision results do not add uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds concrete selection results: Pythia scores 48.5 with min-DiME versus 45.5 using its final layer, whereas LLM2Vec scores 60.0 versus 63.9 respectively. Figure 14 substantially replaces the vision results under changed probing conditions and adds AIMv2 findings. These are newly reported or replaced outcomes, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix F becomes G with substantive local revisions: Proposition 1 changes from a one-sided inner-product bound to an absolute-inner-product bound and receives a rewritten argument. Theorem 6 revises its displayed entropy expression and changes the probability exponent's denominator from N^6 to N^8. The effective-rank and InfoNCE theorems remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a unified representation-quality framework, useful intermediate representations, autoregressive compression bottlenecks across domains, and representation changes associated with CoT finetuning. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds a multimodal-pretraining hypothesis to explain why AIMv2 has an entropy valley without improved intermediate-layer accuracy, qualifying the earlier association between these phenomena. v2 also explicitly leaves intrinsic-dimensionality analysis and formal integration of anisotropy to future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link and documents that Figure 14 uses a common 24-layer ViT-L architecture with attention probes on frozen backbone tokens. The shared architecture is newly disclosed; v1 does not provide enough detail to establish an actual architecture change.

R1.justification: The research positioning expands substantially through discussions of attention sinks, intrinsic dimensionality, anisotropy, and pretext-task theory, citing work such as Barbero, Cheng, Valeriani, Razzhigaev, and Saponati. Further links connect residual behavior and early-layer specialization to Csordas and Zhao. These add substantive relationships to prior research beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, experimental narration, vision discussion, and conclusion receive localized rewrites, and related-work paragraphs are reorganized. New Appendix E shifts the existing extreme-prompt, theorem, and visualization appendices to F–H. Publication information and acknowledgements are updated, while the overall narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: Presentation changes are localized but clear: Table 2 is added, and Figure 14 changes from a small three-panel raster plot to a larger four-panel display with revised axes, legends, and a detailed caption. Several retained figures and tables are resized or relocated without changing their results.

improvement.justification: Appendix E and Table 2 make the proposed metrics' practical usefulness directly assessable, while the revised vision comparison reveals the AIMv2 exception. Added code-access information and experimental details improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by mixed selector performance, conflicting ImageNet-100/ImageNet-1k descriptions, and an inconsistent probability inequality in the revised Proposition 1 proof. The empirical and documentation gains support a limited overall improvement.
